children: First-time homebuyers could get up to $50,000 from the federal government for a down payment on a house under a new bill introduced by Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-OR) and cosponsored by Sen. Ron Wyden (D-OR).

The Homeownership Promise Act would create Homeownership Promise Accounts to help first-time homebuyers save for a house. For each dollar put into the account, the federal government would contribute $5.

The overall contribution limit would be $60,000 – $10,000 maximum personal contributions in addition to $50,000 maximum federal matching funds. These funds can be used to purchase a median-priced home.
Employers and nonprofits would also be able to make contributions to the accounts on an individual's behalf.

"For millions of young Americans, homeownership remains further out of reach than ever before," Merkley said, adding that his bill would "restore the promise of homeownership—one of the foundations that working families need to thrive—by allowing all Americans to save for a home and live that piece of the American Dream."
The median age of first-time homebuyers reached an an all-time high of 40 years, according to a 2025 report from the National Association of Realtors. That's up from 31 years in 2015.
While it's unlikely that Merkley's bill will move forward in the Republican-controlled Congress, it could gain traction if Democrats regain control of Congress after the midterms.
To note, Congress passed the 21st Century
earlier this year, which aims to boost housing supply and address affordability challenges.
